info.title: distribute.you MCP Service
info.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for distribute.you. Exposes campaign management tools via MCP protocol over HTTP.

distribute_status.description: Check the connection and say who the key belongs to: the user, and every organization the key reaches with its brands. A key belongs to its USER and reaches every organization that user is a member of; it never belongs to a brand. Call this first: the other tools take a brandId (and an orgId when a brand sits in several organizations) from this list. Then, before acting on what the client asks (set something up, change how a campaign behaves, launch, attach files, caps...), read the method: distribute_list_skills, then distribute_read_skill on `index` and on every skill whose description matches the ask. They are the steps our own Copilot follows; an API route alone rarely is the whole setup. A key that reaches many organizations (a distribute.you staff key reaches all of them) should pass `search` with a name or domain ("acme", "acme.com") to get only the organizations and brands that match. Keys are created and revoked at https://dashboard.distribute.you and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

search.description: Only the organizations whose id or name contains this text, or that hold a brand whose id, name or domain contains it (case-insensitive).

distribute_list_skills.description: List the method skills: how to organize a client's request on distribute.you (offers and their documents, the catalogue, sales funnels, campaigns and their caps, triggers, billing, workflows and plays...), the same skills our own Copilot follows. Each skill has a `slug`, a `title`, and a `description` saying when to read it; `parentSlug` places it in the tree (root: `index`). Read this BEFORE acting on a client ask, then read `index` and every matching skill with distribute_read_skill. Free, read-only, the same for every client: names no brand or organization.

distribute_read_skill.description: Read one method skill in full (markdown `content`): the steps, the API operations to call in order and the traps. Start with `index`, then the skills distribute_list_skills shows matching the client's ask. Follow them; run the operations they name with distribute_call_api (distribute_describe_api for their parameters). Free, read-only.

distribute_signup_start.description: No human needed: request a key with an email, prepay when you need to spend. Step 1 of 2 to open a distribute.you account and get an API key, with no key and no dashboard. Give an email you can read and a phone number in international format (+33612345678; only its format is checked). A 6-digit code is emailed; then call distribute_signup_complete with it. An email that already has an account works too: it gets one more key for that account. Free to call. Pay as you go: you prepay a balance when you want to spend (distribute_prepay), and each action is billed at its price on https://distribute.you/catalog.

email.description: Email to open the account with. The code is sent there.

phone.description: Phone number in international format, e.g. +33612345678. Only its format is checked.

distribute_signup_complete.description: Step 2 of 2: send the 6-digit code emailed by distribute_signup_start and get an API key. This MCP session uses the new key at once (when it had none), so every other tool works right after. Keep `apiKey`: it is shown once. To use it later, reconnect this MCP server with the header `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, or call https://api.distribute.you with that header. Each call makes a NEW key. Reading the account is free; anything that spends needs a prepaid balance first (distribute_prepay).

keyName.description: A name for the key, to recognize it later (e.g. the agent's name).

distribute_prepay.description: No human needed: request a key with an email, prepay when you need to spend. Prepay before calls that spend money (a call that needs money and finds none answers 402 payment_required). Returns a payment `url`: open it, or give it to your human to pay by card. The card is saved and reloads the balance automatically: when the balance falls under `auto_topup_threshold_cents`, it adds `auto_topup_amount_cents`. Auto top-up is required. Amounts in cents, minimums: topup_amount_cents 1000 ($10), auto_topup_amount_cents 1500 ($15), auto_topup_threshold_cents 500 ($5). Less is refused with `amount_below_minimum`, naming the field. Pay as you go: each action is billed from the balance at its price on https://distribute.you/catalog (an email sent is priced by its BounceVerify verdict). What a campaign may spend is its own cap, set on the campaign. Then check distribute_prepaid_status until `state` is `active`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

topup_amount_cents.description: First prepayment, in cents. At least 1000 ($10).

auto_topup_amount_cents.description: Amount added at each automatic reload, in cents. At least 1500 ($15).

auto_topup_threshold_cents.description: Balance under which the card reloads, in cents. At least 500 ($5).

cancel_url.description: Page shown if payment is cancelled (default https://distribute.you/?prepaid=cancelled).

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_prepaid_status.description: Read the prepaid account: `state` (awaiting_payment: not paid yet; active: ready to spend; card_not_reloadable or auto_topup_off: fix it with distribute_prepay; not_prepaid), `balance_cents`, `paid_cents`, the automatic reload settings and whether the saved card can reload. Free to call. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

distribute_list_workflows.description: List all available workflows. Includes styled workflows written in the style of industry experts (e.g. Hormozi). Which workflow runs on a step is never picked by you or the client: the platform ranks the workflows of each step like a multi-armed bandit (the best return on spend runs, newer ones still get tried until measured). A step that must behave a certain way is a play (distribute_read_skill `catalogue-plays`). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

human_id.description: Filter by human expert ID (for styled workflows)

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_list_campaigns.description: List the campaigns of one brand or organization. A campaign is one sales funnel run for one offer of a brand, started or paused as a whole. Each campaign has a name, a status (`ongoing` = running, `stopped` = paused), a type (`proactive`: it reaches out to new people on its own; `reactive`: it acts when something happens, such as a reply), and its caps: a max budget and/or a max volume per period, in words in `budget` and `volume` ("Max $10/day", "Up to 50 leads handled/week"), with what the current period used in `maxBudget` and `maxVolume`. A campaign with no max budget spends nothing. Report each campaign by its name. Each campaign also says what starts it, in `runsWhen` ("Each time: Email Pushed Via API" for a reactive campaign, with its `trigger` {slug, name}; "On its own, within its caps (no trigger)" for a proactive one), and what it does, in `path` (its steps in order, e.g. "Lead → Sales Cold Email Outreach → Positive reply → Paid client"; the outcome names are the platform's own, read as served). Every trigger a campaign can start on, and which ones you may fire: distribute_list_triggers. Before telling the client something is missing, read the running (`ongoing`) campaigns: one may already do what they ask (e.g. send an email they wrote: a running campaign that runs "Each time: Email Pushed Via API"). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

status.description: Filter by campaign status: `ongoing` (running) or `stopped`. `all`, or no status, returns every campaign. Any other value is refused.

distribute_campaign_stats.description: Get one campaign's results: pass `campaignId`, the campaign id from distribute_list_campaigns (the older name `campaign_id` still works). A campaign runs as one; its results come in `results`, one entry per outcome it brings in (`outcome`, such as Positive reply or Lead; `bringsIn` is the older name of the same value) with the channel doing it (`channel`). An id seen elsewhere (trigger events, offer stats, a lead's `campaignId`) is one step of a campaign: pass it too, the answer names its campaign in `note`. Report the campaign by its name and never call an entry of `results` a campaign. Report meetings, positive replies and delivery rate first, then volume and cost; bounces and other failures last. Each entry is ordered that way: `headline`, then `summary`, then the raw figures, then `failureDetails`. Show zeros plainly (0 meetings is still reported). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

campaign_id.description: Older name of `campaignId`, still accepted. Prefer `campaignId`.

distribute_suggest_icp.description: Analyze a brand's website and suggest an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Use this when the user doesn't know who to target and wants AI-generated targeting suggestions. Returns a description of the ideal customers to aim a campaign at. Name the brand by brandId, or by brand_url (matched against the brands of the targeted organization). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brand_url.description: The brand/company URL to analyze for ICP extraction. Optional when brandId is given.

distribute_list_leads.description: List the leads (prospects, people we found and contacted) of a brand, newest first, with where each one stands: contacted, sent, delivered, clicked, replied (and how the reply was classified), bounced, unsubscribed, with dates. Each lead carries an `id` (this lead on one campaign) to pass to distribute_get_lead for its emails and conversation, and a `leadId` (the person, the id trigger events and emails name; distribute_get_lead takes it too). Pages with `cursor`: pass the `nextCursor` of the previous page. `total` is the brand's lead count. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose leads to list (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

campaignId.description: Only leads of this campaign part (a lead's `campaignId`).

distribute_list_emails.description: List the cold emails we wrote and sent for a brand: for each prospect, the first email and every follow-up (`subject`, then `sequence`: one entry per step with its `bodyText`, its `kind` (first_email or follow_up) and its send `status`: `sent` at `sentAt`, `queued` (goes out in the prospect's business hours) or `stopped` (will not go out: reply, bounce, opt-out, meeting, sequence stopped)), with who it went to (`leadEmail`, lead name, title, company, `leadId`). Use it to answer "what did you send for my brand, and what is still queued". Replies and delivery are on distribute_list_leads / distribute_get_lead. Pages with `limit` and `offset`. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

brandId.description: Brand whose emails to list (from distribute_status).

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

campaignId.description: Only the emails of this campaign part.

distribute_get_lead.description: Everything about ONE lead in one call: who they are and where they stand (sent, delivered, replied...), the emails we wrote for them (first email and follow-ups, subject and body, each with its send status: sent at sentAt, queued or stopped), and the conversation (every message we sent and every reply they wrote, oldest first). Pass `leadId`: either a lead's `id` from distribute_list_leads (this lead on one campaign), or the person's id: a list row's `leadId`, or the `ranLeads[].leadId` a trigger event (POST /v1/trigger-events) answers. With the person's id, also pass `campaignId` (the `ranLeads[].campaignId` beside it, or a lead's `campaignId`) or brandId, so the lead is read directly on that campaign (with only a brandId, among the brand's newest 1,000 leads); the answer's `lead.id` is then the lead's `id`. The older name `lead_id` still works. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

leadId.description: A lead's `id` from distribute_list_leads, or the person's id (a list row's `leadId`, a trigger event's `ranLeads[].leadId`). Required (or `lead_id`).

lead_id.description: Older name of `leadId`, still accepted. Prefer `leadId`.

campaignId.description: With a person's id: the campaign step they are on (`ranLeads[].campaignId` of the trigger event, or a lead's `campaignId`).

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

distribute_list_triggers.description: List the triggers: the entry doors a reactive campaign starts on, each with its `id`, `name`, what it means, its `type` (`outcome`: an outcome just reached for a person, named by `outcome`; `condition`: computed by us) and `callable`. Outcome triggers (an outcome was just reached for a person: Form submitted, Meeting booked, Paid client...) are callable: fire one when that fact happens in the client's own tools. Condition triggers computed by us (an outcome + a delay + "still not" another, a GitHub issue in prod...) are never fired by a call: report the outcome they wait on instead, they follow from it. Each trigger's `callable` decides: fire only one with `callable: true`. A new outcome or trigger is a feature request to the distribute.you team, never created by a call. To fire a callable one for a person when the fact happens ("a form was submitted by jane@acme.com"): distribute_call_api POST /v1/trigger-events with body {triggerId, brandId, offerId, person: {email, name?}, item?, idempotencyKey?} (the brand's offers: GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers). Every live campaign of that offer starting on the trigger runs for the person, within its caps; the answer's `event.outcome` says `ran` or `skipped` with the reason (`no_campaign`: no campaign starts on it; `campaign_off`: the ones that do are paused). A `callable: false` trigger is refused before the call: tell the user it is computed by us and fires on its own, and offer to report the outcome it `followsFrom` if that really happened. The same for every client: names no brand or organization. Free, read-only.

distribute_find_api.description: Find how to do something in distribute.you when no other tool covers it. Searches every operation of the distribute.you API (the same API and the same scope your key has: leads, emails, conversations, campaigns and their caps, offers, sales funnels, triggers, billing, CRM, stats...) by what you want to do, in plain words ("list the emails sent for my brand", "set a campaign's max budget", "pause a campaign", "account balance"). Returns the best matching operations (method, path, summary, required parameters). Then call distribute_describe_api for the details and distribute_call_api to run it. With no query, lists the areas of the API and how many operations each has. To list the triggers (and which ones a call may fire), use distribute_list_triggers.

query.description: What you want to do, in plain words.

area.description: Restrict to one area (as listed with no query), e.g. Leads, Emails, Billing.

distribute_describe_api.description: Read one distribute.you API operation in full before calling it: what it does, its path and query parameters (required or not), the JSON body it takes, and `answers`: what a successful call returns (per status, the JSON shape with each field's meaning), so you can act on the answer. Name it by `operationId`, or by `method` and `path`, as distribute_find_api returned them.

path.description: Path template (/v1/leads/{id}) or a concrete path.

distribute_call_api.description: Call any distribute.you API operation with your key, exactly as the API would answer it (same scope, same refusals). Use it for anything the other tools do not cover; find the operation with distribute_find_api first. `path` is the concrete path with its ids filled in (/v1/leads/123/timeline); query parameters go in `query`, a JSON body in `body`. Writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) change the account for real: say what you are about to change before calling. Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

body.description: JSON body for POST, PUT and PATCH.

brandId.description: Brand to act on (from distribute_status). Selects the organization holding it. Required when your key reaches several organizations, unless orgId is given.

orgId.description: Organization to act in (from distribute_status). Add it when a brand sits in several organizations, or to act in an organization without naming a brand.

Report the campaign by its name and never call an entry of `results` a campaign. Report meetings, positive replies and delivery rate first, then volume and cost; bounces and other failures last. Each entry is ordered that way: `headline`, then `summary`, then the raw figures, then `failureDetails`. Show zeros plainly (0 meetings is still reported). Call distribute_status first to list brands, then pass brandId (and orgId if a brand sits in several orgs). A user in a single organization can omit both.

post.summary: List the triggers: the entry doors a reactive campaign starts on, each with its `id`, `name`, what it means, its `type` (`outcome`: an outcome just reached for a person, named by `outcome`; `condition`: computed by us) and `callable`. Outcome triggers (an outcome was just reached for a person: Form submitted, Meeting booked, Paid client...) are callable: fire one when that fact happens in the client's own tools. Condition triggers computed by us (an outcome + a delay + "still not" another, a GitHub issue in prod...) are never fired by a call: report the outcome they wait on instead, they follow from it. Each trigger's `callable` decides: fire only one with `callable: true`. A new outcome or trigger is a feature request to the distribute.you team, never created by a call. To fire a callable one for a person when the fact happens ("a form was submitted by jane@acme.com"): distribute_call_api POST /v1/trigger-events with body {triggerId, brandId, offerId, person: {email, name?}, item?, idempotencyKey?} (the brand's offers: GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers). Every live campaign of that offer starting on the trigger runs for the person, within its caps; the answer's `event.outcome` says `ran` or `skipped` with the reason (`no_campaign`: no campaign starts on it; `campaign_off`: the ones that do are paused). A `callable: false` trigger is refused before the call: tell the user it is computed by us and fires on its own, and offer to report the outcome it `followsFrom` if that really happened. The same for every client: names no brand or organization. Free, read-only.

post.summary: Find how to do something in distribute.you when no other tool covers it. Returns the best matching operations (method, path, summary, required parameters). Then call distribute_describe_api for the details and distribute_call_api to run it. With no query, lists the areas of the API and how many operations each has. To list the triggers (and which ones a call may fire), use distribute_list_triggers.
